The Black Death was a pandemic of bubonic plague that swept through Europe, the Middle East and North Africa from 1346 to 1353, killing perhaps a third to half of the people there. It is one of the deadliest events in human history.

The cause was the bacterium Yersinia pestis, carried by fleas on rats and other animals. DNA from graves near Lake Issyk-Kul in Central Asia shows the plague was there by 1338. It moved west along the trade routes that the Mongol conquests had opened.

  • In 1346 it struck the army of the Golden Horde besieging the Genoese port of Caffa in Crimea.
  • Italian ships carried it into the Mediterranean in 1347, to Constantinople, Sicily and Egypt.
  • By 1351 it had crossed most of Europe, and it reached Russia by 1353.
  • In the Middle East it ravaged Cairo, the capital of Mamluk Egypt, and spread across Syria and Arabia.

Its course in China and India is poorly recorded, and whether it caused great deaths there is uncertain.

The shock changed European society. With so many dead, workers were scarce and wages rose, which weakened serfdom in western Europe. Fear drove waves of violence against Jews, who were falsely blamed for poisoning wells, and bands of flagellants whipped themselves in public. The plague came back again and again for centuries, the last great outbreak in western Europe being the plague of Marseille in 1720. It was the second great plague pandemic, after the Plague of Justinian.
sum: The Black Death was a pandemic of bubonic plague that swept through Europe, the Middle East and North Africa from 1346 to 1353, killing perhaps a third to half of the people there. It is one of the deadliest events in human history.
